title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Charred yogurt-marinated chicken in a silky, warmly spiced tomato and cream sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
Fresh cilantro and cooked basmati rice, for serving
instructions: Combine the chicken with yogurt, garlic, ginger, one teaspoon garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and half the salt, coating every piece before chilling for at least one hour.
Heat a heavy skillet over high heat with one tablespoon oil, then sear the marinated chicken in uncrowded batches until dark charred patches develop on several sides.
Transfer the browned chicken to a clean plate; it may remain slightly underdone because it will finish safely while simmering later in the prepared masala sauce.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and onion, and cook slowly until deeply golden before stirring in tomato paste, chili powder, and remaining garam masala.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, scrape the flavorful browned residue from the skillet, and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens and loses its raw tomato aroma.
Blend the sauce carefully until smooth if desired, return it to gentle heat, and stir in the cream and butter without allowing the dairy-rich mixture to boil aggressively.
Return the chicken and collected juices to the sauce, then simmer gently until every piece reaches 165°F and the sauce clings generously to the meat.
Taste and adjust the remaining salt, scatter fresh cilantro over the finished curry, and serve immediately with hot basmati rice or warm naan for dipping.
tips: Marinate for at least one hour for seasoned, tender chicken.
Sear in batches so the meat chars instead of steaming.
Keep the cream sauce at a gentle simmer.
commonMistakes: Crowding the skillet prevents proper browning.
Boiling after adding cream can split the sauce.
Using chicken breast without adjusting time can dry it out.
substitutions: Use mild paprika when Kashmiri chili is unavailable.
Use coconut cream for a different dairy-free finish.
Chicken breast may be used but should be monitored closely.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
Freeze cooled curry for up to 2 months.
Reheat gently to 165°F, adding a splash of water if needed.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Curry
description: Home-style chicken curry with tender thighs in a deeply aromatic onion and tomato gravy.
instructions: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season them lightly with some of the measured salt so their surfaces can brown rather than steam when they reach the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide heavy pan, brown the chicken in batches on both sides, and transfer the pieces to a clean plate while preparing the gravy.
Add the sliced onions to the same pan and cook patiently, stirring and scraping often, until they soften and become a deep, even golden brown.
Stir in garlic and ginger for one minute, then add turmeric, coriander, cumin, chili powder, and one teaspoon garam masala before the aromatics can scorch.
Add the chopped tomatoes and remaining salt, cooking until the tomatoes collapse and the oil begins to separate visibly around the concentrated onion-spice mixture.
Return the chicken and any resting juices, pour in the hot water, and simmer partially covered until the meat is tender and reaches a safe internal temperature of 165°F.
Whisk the yogurt until smooth, temper it with a little hot gravy, then stir it gradually into the pan over low heat to maintain a cohesive, creamy sauce.
Finish with the remaining garam masala and cilantro, rest the curry for five minutes, and serve with basmati rice after checking the final salt and consistency.
tips: Brown onions deeply for a full-flavored gravy.
Temper yogurt before adding it to the hot pan.
Bone-in thighs remain juicy during the simmer.
commonMistakes: Rushing the onions leaves the sauce thin and sharp.
Adding cold yogurt over high heat can curdle it.
Stopping before the chicken reaches 165°F is unsafe.
substitutions: Use boneless thighs and reduce simmering time.
Use canned chopped tomatoes when fresh are poor.
Use mild paprika for a less spicy curry.
storage: Refrigerate promptly for up to 4 days.
Freeze airtight portions for up to 3 months.
Reheat thoroughly to 165°F before serving.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef Wellington
description: Beef tenderloin wrapped with mushroom duxelles, prosciutto, and crisp golden puff pastry.
ingredients: 2 egg yolks, beaten with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Tie the tenderloin into an even cylinder, season it with measured salt and pepper, then sear every surface in very hot olive oil until deeply browned outside.
Remove the beef from the pan, brush it immediately with English mustard while warm, and refrigerate until fully cool before wrapping so the pastry stays crisp.
Pulse mushrooms and garlic into fine crumbs, then cook them with butter and thyme until every trace of moisture evaporates and the duxelles forms a dry paste.
Overlap prosciutto on plastic wrap, spread the cooled mushroom mixture evenly over it, and roll the chilled beef tightly inside before refrigerating for thirty minutes.
Roll the puff pastry just large enough to enclose the beef, remove the plastic, and wrap the cylinder tightly while trimming excessive pastry and sealing the seam underneath.
Brush the parcel with egg wash, chill it for another twenty minutes, then score the surface decoratively without cutting through and apply a second thin glaze.
Bake at 425°F until the pastry is deeply golden and the beef center registers about 125–130°F for medium-rare, checking with an instant-read thermometer.
Rest the Wellington for at least fifteen minutes so its juices settle, then cut thick slices with a sharp serrated knife and serve while the pastry remains crisp.
tips: Cook the mushroom mixture until completely dry.
Chill after every wrapping stage.
Use a thermometer to control beef doneness.
commonMistakes: Warm beef melts pastry before baking.
Wet duxelles creates a soggy inner layer.
Cutting immediately releases juices into the crust.
substitutions: Use chestnut mushrooms instead of cremini.
Use Parma ham in place of prosciutto.
Dijon mustard can replace English mustard.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat slices in a 350°F oven until hot.
Avoid microwaving because it softens the pastry.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Steak and Kidney Pie
description: Traditional steak and kidney pie with tender meat, dark savory gravy, and flaky pastry.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
8 oz lamb kidneys, trimmed and cut into pieces
instructions: Trim the kidneys carefully, removing the white cores, then pat both meats dry and season them evenly with the measured salt and black pepper.
Toss the beef and kidney with flour, shake away the excess, and brown the pieces in hot oil in several small batches so a dark crust develops.
Transfer the browned meat to a clean bowl, lower the heat, and cook the onion until soft before stirring in tomato paste until it darkens slightly.
Add Worcestershire sauce and beef stock while scraping the pan thoroughly, then return the meat with thyme and bay leaf and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for about ninety minutes until the beef is tender, then uncover and reduce the gravy until thick enough to coat the meat generously.
Discard the bay leaf, cool the filling completely, and spoon it into a deep pie dish because warm filling will melt the butter in the pastry prematurely.
Cover with puff pastry, press and crimp the edge securely, cut steam vents, and brush the top evenly with beaten egg for a glossy golden finish.
Bake at 400°F for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is fully risen and deeply browned, then rest for ten minutes before serving the hot filling.
tips: Remove the tough kidney cores before cooking.
Cool the filling fully before adding pastry.
Reduce the gravy so the pie slices cleanly.
commonMistakes: Crowding meat prevents proper browning.
Thin gravy makes the pastry base soggy.
Sealing pastry without vents traps excess steam.
substitutions: Use ox kidney instead of lamb kidney.
Use shortcrust pastry for a firmer lid.
Replace thyme with a small amount of rosemary.
storage: Refrigerate covered leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a 350°F oven until piping hot.
Freeze the cooled filling separately for up to 3 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Cottage Pie
description: Rich minced beef and vegetables beneath a crisp, buttery mashed-potato topping.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Place the potatoes in cold salted water, bring them to a steady boil, and cook until completely tender when pierced so the finished mash will remain smooth.
Drain thoroughly, let steam escape, then mash with butter, warm milk, and half the salt until creamy without overworking the potato starch.
Heat oil in a wide pan, brown the ground beef thoroughly while breaking it into small pieces, and drain excessive fat only if a large amount collects.
Add onion and carrots, cook until softened, then stir in garlic and tomato paste and continue cooking until the paste darkens and smells sweet.
Add Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and remaining salt, then simmer uncovered until the liquid reduces to a rich gravy that supports the topping.
Fold in the frozen peas, transfer the filling to a baking dish, and allow it to cool briefly so the potato can be spread without sinking.
Spoon mashed potato over the filling, seal it completely to the dish edges, roughen the top with a fork, and scatter the cheddar evenly.
Bake at 400°F for about 25 minutes until bubbling and golden, broil briefly if needed, then rest for ten minutes before serving clean portions.
tips: Steam-dry potatoes before mashing.
Reduce the beef gravy until thick.
Rough potato ridges create crisp browned edges.
commonMistakes: Using lamb turns the dish into shepherd's pie.
Watery filling causes layers to collapse.
Overmixing potatoes makes them gluey.
substitutions: Use Yukon Gold potatoes for a richer mash.
Replace cheddar with Parmesan.
Use fresh peas added near the end.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 4 days.
Freeze baked portions for up to 2 months.
Reheat to 165°F in the oven or microwave.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: Savory minced lamb and vegetables baked beneath fluffy golden mashed potatoes.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water until they are completely fork-tender, then drain well and return them briefly to the warm pot to release steam.
Mash with warm cream, half the butter, Parmesan, and part of the measured salt until smooth, then cover so the topping remains spreadable.
Brown the ground lamb in a large skillet, breaking it apart thoroughly, and carefully drain excessive rendered fat while leaving enough to cook the vegetables.
Add onion and carrots and cook until tender, then stir in garlic, flour, and tomato paste and cook for one minute to remove raw flavors.
Gradually add broth and Worcestershire sauce while stirring, then season with rosemary, thyme, and remaining salt and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Fold in the frozen peas, spread the lamb mixture evenly in a baking dish, and cool it for several minutes so the potato topping stays distinct.
Spoon the mashed potatoes over the filling, seal the edges, texture the surface with a fork, and dot the remaining butter over the ridges.
Bake at 400°F until bubbling and golden for 25 to 30 minutes, then rest ten minutes before serving so each portion holds together.
tips: Use lamb, not beef, for traditional shepherd's pie.
Warm dairy keeps the mash smooth.
Cool the filling briefly before topping.
commonMistakes: Leaving excess lamb fat makes the filling greasy.
A thin gravy allows the layers to mingle.
A flat potato surface browns less attractively.
substitutions: Use Yukon Gold potatoes for the topping.
Replace Parmesan with mature cheddar.
Use fresh rosemary at half the quantity.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days.
Freeze tightly wrapped portions for up to 2 months.
Reheat until the center reaches 165°F.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Lancashire Hotpot
description: Slow-baked Lancashire lamb and onions under overlapping crisp golden potato slices.
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Pat the lamb dry, season it with salt and pepper, dust with the measured flour, and shake away loose flour that could burn during browning.
Heat oil in a large ovenproof casserole and brown the lamb in small batches, developing color on every side before transferring it to a clean plate.
Cook the onions and carrots in the same casserole until lightly golden, scraping the base so the browned meat residue flavors the vegetables.
Return the lamb, add Worcestershire sauce, stock, bay leaves, and thyme, and bring the liquid just to a simmer before turning off the heat.
Arrange the thin potato slices in tightly overlapping circles across the entire surface, creating an even lid that protects the meat as it slowly braises.
Brush the potatoes with melted butter, cover the casserole, and bake at 325°F for ninety minutes until the lamb is tender beneath the potato layer.
Remove the lid, increase the oven to 400°F, and bake another 30 to 40 minutes until the exposed potato edges are crisp and richly golden.
Rest the hotpot for ten minutes, remove the bay leaves when encountered, and serve by lifting through both crisp potato and tender lamb layers.
tips: Lamb shoulder becomes tender during slow baking.
Slice potatoes evenly for uniform cooking.
Uncover only for the final browning stage.
commonMistakes: Lean lamb cuts can dry during the long bake.
Thick potato slices may remain firm.
Too much stock prevents the potato base from setting.
substitutions: Use lamb neck fillet instead of shoulder.
Use beef stock when lamb stock is unavailable.
Use Maris Piper potatoes in place of russets.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days.
Reheat uncovered at 350°F until 165°F.
Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef and Ale Pie
description: Tender beef and vegetables in dark ale gravy beneath burnished flaky pastry.
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, coat it lightly in flour, and shake off the excess so the cubes brown cleanly without leaving scorched flour behind.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and brown the beef in several batches, giving every cube room to develop a dark crust before transferring it aside.
Cook the onion and carrots until softened, then stir in garlic and tomato paste and continue until the paste deepens in color and smells caramelized.
Pour in the ale and scrape the casserole thoroughly, simmering for several minutes to reduce its sharp alcoholic aroma before adding the stock.
Return the beef with Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaf, cover loosely, and simmer gently until the meat is fork-tender, about ninety minutes.
Uncover and reduce the gravy until thick, discard the bay leaf, and cool the complete filling so its heat cannot melt the puff pastry before baking.
Transfer to a pie dish, cover with pastry, crimp securely, cut steam vents, and brush evenly with beaten egg for a burnished, crisp finish.
Bake at 400°F for 30 to 35 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling, then rest for ten minutes before spooning out the rich filling.
tips: Choose an ale you enjoy drinking.
Brown beef in uncrowded batches.
Cool filling before covering with pastry.
commonMistakes: Very bitter ale can dominate the gravy.
Thin filling produces a soggy crust.
Warm filling melts pastry layers.
substitutions: Use stout for a darker roasted flavor.
Use shortcrust pastry instead of puff pastry.
Replace thyme with a small rosemary sprig.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a 350°F oven until piping hot.
Freeze the cooled filling for up to 3 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken and Leek Pie
description: Tender chicken and sweet leeks in creamy herb sauce under crisp puff pastry.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
instructions: Pat the chicken pieces dry, season them with measured salt and pepper, then brown them in hot olive oil in batches without cooking them completely through.
Move the chicken to a clean plate, melt the butter in the same pan, and cook the carefully washed leeks until soft without allowing them to brown heavily.
Stir in the garlic for thirty seconds, sprinkle the flour evenly over the leeks, and cook for one minute so the finished sauce has no raw flour taste.
Add chicken stock gradually while stirring continuously, scraping the pan base and allowing each addition to blend smoothly before pouring in more liquid.
Stir in cream, thyme, and Dijon mustard, return the chicken and juices, and simmer until the meat reaches 165°F and the sauce becomes thick.
Transfer the filling to a pie dish and cool it completely because a hot creamy filling will soften the pastry and prevent distinct flaky layers.
Cover with puff pastry, trim and crimp the edge, cut several steam vents, and brush the entire surface lightly and evenly with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F for about 30 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden and the filling bubbles at the vents, then rest ten minutes before serving.
tips: Wash between leek layers to remove grit.
Use thighs for moist, flavorful chicken.
Cool the creamy filling before adding pastry.
commonMistakes: Unwashed leeks can leave sand in the pie.
Thin sauce makes the pastry soggy.
Overcooking chicken before baking dries it out.
substitutions: Use chicken breast and shorten simmering time.
Use whole milk for a lighter sauce.
Replace thyme with chopped tarragon.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Reheat in a 350°F oven until 165°F.
Freeze the cooled filling separately for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Fish Pie
description: White fish and salmon with peas in creamy parsley sauce beneath golden mashed potatoes.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1/2 cup whole milk, plus 2 cups for poaching
12 oz cod fillet, cut into chunks
8 oz salmon fillet, cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until completely tender, drain and steam-dry them, then mash with two tablespoons butter and half a cup warm milk.
Place cod and salmon in a wide pan with two cups milk and the bay leaf, then poach very gently until barely opaque so the fish does not become dry.
Lift the fish onto a plate with a slotted spoon, strain and reserve the poaching milk, and discard the bay leaf while keeping the fish in large flakes.
Melt the remaining butter, soften the onion without browning, stir in flour for one minute, then gradually whisk in the reserved warm poaching milk.
Simmer the sauce until thick, remove it from direct heat, and stir in parsley, Dijon mustard, peas, remaining salt, and black pepper.
Fold the poached fish through the sauce as gently as possible, transfer everything to a baking dish, and allow the filling to cool for several minutes.
Spread mashed potato over the filling to seal the edges, create fork ridges across the surface, and scatter the grated cheddar evenly on top.
Bake at 400°F for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and golden, then rest for ten minutes so the creamy filling settles before serving.
tips: Poach fish only until barely opaque.
Keep fish pieces large while folding.
Fork ridges encourage crisp golden peaks.
commonMistakes: Boiling the fish makes it tough.
A thin sauce causes a watery pie.
Skipping the rest makes portions spread.
substitutions: Use haddock instead of cod.
Add smoked haddock for deeper flavor.
Replace cheddar with Parmesan.
storage: Refrigerate promptly for up to 2 days.
Reheat to 165°F only once.
Freeze assembled unbaked pie for up to 1 month.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
